ren_lv1_night_ward_1: The ward corridor was quiet at night.
The lights of the nurses' station reflected on the floor, and an occasional monitor beep sounded in the distance.
Sakaguchi had just finished a round of the wards.
Ren sat at the nurses' station organizing handover notes. In front of her was an open sandwich box, with only half a sandwich left inside.
“Ah, Dr. Sakaguchi. I finally caught you.”
“You make it sound as if I've done something wrong.”
“Not at all. But I've been looking for you for quite a while.”
She glanced at the duty roster on the desk and suddenly smiled.
“Come to think of it, when you first arrived at Hoshimi, the director assigned me to be your partner.”
“Of course I remember. Why bring that up all of a sudden?”
“Since we happen to be working the night shift together, let me say this properly—”
“I look forward to working with you!”
She gave a small, earnest bow.
“Why so formal all of a sudden?”
Then she quickly added something else.
“But while I have the chance, there's one thing I need to make clear.”
“Being your dedicated nurse is a work assignment. I'm not your personal secretary.”
“Someone once asked me whether being a regular partner meant I could also remind the doctor to eat, find his glasses, and tidy his desk.”
“Though I might actually need your help remembering to eat.”
Sakaguchi glanced at the handover notes beside her.
“Let's get down to business. Did you come looking for me because a patient needs attention?”
“Yes. There's something I'd like you to check personally.”
She pushed the sandwich aside and pulled out a chart.
“Do you remember the patient scheduled for a local excision of a breast mass tomorrow morning?”
“I do. I reviewed her imaging and surgical plan this afternoon.”
She laid several records side by side on the desk.
“The examination report and the surgery booking say right side. So does the consent form the patient signed.”
“But this nursing handover note from this evening says left side.”
Sakaguchi looked where she was pointing.
It was exactly as she said.
“Possibly. But I don't want to assume it's just a clerical error.”
“I have. She said she remembered it being the right side, but after seeing this note, she wasn't sure anymore.”
“But I don't think she really is.”
“When I checked her evening preparations, she folded that handover note, opened it again, and looked at it several times.”
“No. She only told me after I asked whether something was worrying her.”
“Let's check the original imaging and surgical plan again. I'll go to the ward with you.”
“Didn't you say she still seemed worried?”
“I thought you'd say we should leave it until tomorrow morning.”
“We'll check again as part of the preoperative process tomorrow. But now that we've found conflicting records tonight, we shouldn't leave them unresolved.”
“Besides, the patient needs to be able to sleep.”
The lights in the ward had already been dimmed.
An adult woman in the bed by the window was still awake.
Hearing their footsteps, she hurriedly sat up a little.
“Ah… Doctor. I'm sorry to make you come over so late.”
“It's all right. Nurse Nanase told me you still had some questions about tomorrow's operation.”
She glanced at Ren standing by the bed.
“The handover note really does say left side. That's why we're checking it again.”
“But… I remember it being the right side.”
“Yes. We've just rechecked the original imaging, medical record, and consent form. The surgical plan is for the right side.”
“Then why does that paper say left?”

“There is an error in the nursing handover note. We're checking and correcting it according to procedure, and we'll notify everyone concerned. Before surgery tomorrow, the whole team will again confirm your identity, the operation, and the site.”
“I thought perhaps I was the one who remembered it wrong.”
“But the doctors are so busy, and I don't understand much of this. I thought… maybe it was just another way of writing it.”
“Left and right can't be different ways of writing the same thing.”
She said it with complete seriousness.
The patient was startled for a moment, then smiled a little.
“If there's anything else you don't understand, you can ask now.”
The patient hesitated for a moment.
“Then… will the scar be very noticeable after tomorrow's surgery?”

Sakaguchi sat beside the bed and explained the expected extent of the excision, the incision, possible changes, and which outcomes would depend on what they found during surgery and the later pathology report.
The patient asked a few more questions.
Ren neither spoke for the patient nor hurried her.
Only when the patient momentarily lost her train of thought did Ren softly remind her:
“You also said you wanted to ask when you could return to normal activity after the operation.”
By the time they finished talking, it was nearly midnight.
“I'm sorry I took so much of your time.”
“It wasn't a waste of time. You're the one having surgery tomorrow. It's only right that you understand these things.”
“If you hadn't asked me, I probably would have kept it to myself.”
“…You'll make me blush if you say that.”
This time, she finally gave a natural smile as she spoke.
Ren entered the verification results into the record, corrected the error, and sent the handover notice.
Sakaguchi stood beside her and confirmed that the relevant medical records now agreed.
“Yes. I'll remind everyone again at the morning handover.”
“You didn't see one discrepancy and make a guess, and you didn't stop checking just because the patient said she was fine.”
“Because it was obvious that she cared.”
“I know doctors have a lot to do every day. A single error in a record can look like a very small thing.”
“But it may not be small to the patient.”
She let out a quiet breath.
“Actually, before I called you over, I was worried I might be disturbing you.”
“If something needs the surgeon's confirmation, you should call the surgeon.”
“If you have to worry whether a doctor will be annoyed before you raise a concern, what good is a nurse's question to the surgeon?”
Ren fell quiet for a moment.
Then, as if trying to hide something, she suddenly straightened her back.
“Then I'm really going to be strict with you from now on!”
“If you forget to write your notes, I'll remind you.”
“If the preoperative preparations haven't been checked, I'll keep asking.”
“And if, after an operation, the doctor leaves all the handover work to the nurses—”
“You're a little different from what I imagined.”
“You didn't just correct the handover note and call the matter closed.”
“Didn't you say she was still anxious?”
“…Yes. She kept saying she was fine, but she almost wore that paper out from looking at it.”
“In the end, she asked about the scar and life after surgery.”
“Yes. Those were the things she really wanted to ask but couldn't bring herself to say.”
“You noticed first. I only listened to the rest of what she had to say with you.”
Ren watched him for a while.
“Well then, Dr. Sakaguchi. Since we worked well together tonight, I have a request too.”
“Please don't give me every odd job on the night shift just because I'm usually agreeable.”
She opened the sandwich box that had been waiting for so long.
“I ate half this afternoon. I meant to finish the rest tonight.”
But instead of eating, she looked out at the night beyond the window.
“What do you think of the night shift?”
“I thought you might say something like, ‘The hospital has a special charm at night.’”
“If all the patients sleep well, I'd be happy to admire the night view.”
“When it's quiet, I can give every room a proper look. It's easier to notice when a patient isn't feeling well, too.”
“But once it gets busy, it's hard to find time to rest.”
She looked at the half sandwich.
“So my biggest wish is for every night shift to go safely and peacefully. Ideally, it would be dull enough that I could finish my dinner.”
“The patients sleep well, we do our jobs, and when the time comes, everyone gets to go home as usual.”
Suddenly, a call bell rang beyond the nurses' station.
Ren had just raised the sandwich to her mouth.
They both looked toward the ward corridor.
She slowly put the sandwich back in its box.
“Was the wish I just made a little too extravagant?”
Then she stood up and straightened her nurse's uniform.
She gave Sakaguchi a bright smile.
One behind the other, they walked into the dimly lit ward corridor.
Sakaguchi suddenly thought that another night shift with Ren Nanase probably wouldn't be boring.
At least tonight, he had found a colleague he could trust.
narumi_lv1_beyond_the_resume: 【Hoshimi Hospital · Surgical Office】
The afternoon sunlight slanted into the office.
Sakaguchi was reviewing the day's surgical schedule. His name appeared in the lead surgeon column for the next operation, with Narumi Jinguji listed as first assistant.
Narumi came in carrying two cups of tea.
“It looks like you've seen the schedule.”
“Yes. You'll be my first assistant today?”
“Is there a problem?”
“No. I just thought you were originally going to be the lead surgeon.”
“That was the original plan.”
She set one of the cups in front of Sakaguchi.
“But the director showed me your résumé. Your work at several hospitals overseas, and those rather impressive surgical records.”
“That doesn't sound like a compliment.”
“It is a compliment. It's just…”
She drew out the words, a faint smile on her face.
“When a résumé looks a little too good, I get curious.”
“So you want to see how much I can really do?”
“Exactly.”
“You don't even try to hide it.”
“Don't take it too seriously. I've checked your surgical credentials and the patient's arrangements. This is a normal assignment, not a test using a patient as the exam question.”
She picked up the chart and tapped it lightly on the desk.
“But since we have a chance to operate together, I do want to take a good look.”
“In that case, I'd like to learn from a Hoshimi senior as well.”
“Learn what?”
“What happens here if the lead surgeon ignores the first assistant's opinion?”
“Oh?”
She smiled.
“That depends on how good the surgeon is.”
“I see.”
“Though there's one way your overseas experience won't give you much of an advantage here.”
“Which way?”
“Hoshimi's nurses don't care how many awards you won abroad. If you're vague about an instrument, they'll still make you say exactly what you want.”
“That's reassuring.”
“Why?”
“I prefer a team that's willing to correct the lead surgeon.”
Narumi gave him a brief look.
“…I see.”
She didn't continue the joke. Instead, she turned the chart to the page of examination results.
“Then let's talk about the case.”
【Office · A little later】
“The patient is thirty-two. She has a right ovarian cyst, and her symptoms have persisted for some time. Imaging suggests it's benign, but its size and position led us to recommend surgery.”
Sakaguchi examined the results carefully.
“The plan is to preserve as much normal ovarian tissue as possible.”
“Yes. That matters a great deal to her.”
“It's in the preoperative explanation.”
“She asked me several times whether, if conditions allow, we can remove only the cyst and leave the ovary.”
“What did you tell her?”
“I told her that's our goal, but I can't make an absolute promise before we see the actual situation.”
“Reasonable.”
“After I told her that, she asked again.”
“So you made a separate note of it.”
“The surgical record tells us what we plan to do. Sometimes the patient's words tell us why we need to do it carefully.”
Sakaguchi paused.
“I'll remember that.”
“You're not remembering it for my sake.”
“Of course not.”
Narumi went to the desk and took out a neatly bound research document.
Sakaguchi noticed the author's name on the cover.
“Ryuji Hirasaka…”
Narumi stopped moving for an instant.
“I read his research on female pelvic anatomy and operative field management while I was overseas. The level of detail is genuinely impressive.”
“…Is that so.”
She put the document back on the desk.
“Do you know him?”
“I've read his research.”
That was her entire answer.
At some point, the smile had faded from her face.
Sakaguchi wanted to say something more, but Narumi had already reopened the patient's imaging.
“This area concerns me.”
“Hm?”
“Look here. The tissue planes on the scan may not look exactly the same in surgery. If there are adhesions, we'll need to clear the field first.”
“I was thinking the same thing.”
“Oh?”
“If we can't see clearly at first, there's no need to rush the dissection. We should identify the surrounding tissue, then adjust the traction.”
“Good.”
Her usual lightness returned to her voice.
“At least you sound like more than a doctor with a pretty résumé when we discuss a case.”
“Your standards are strict.”
“I'm being very kind.”
Sakaguchi glanced at the research document set aside on the desk.
He had the vague feeling that the subject had displeased Narumi.
Then again, perhaps she simply had reservations about that researcher's views.
There was no need to press her now.
【Operating Room】
Narumi had administered anesthesia according to the preoperative plan, and all other preparations were complete.
Under the surgical lamps, the team performed its final checks.
“Patient identity, procedure, site, and consent form all match.”
Narumi checked the monitoring data.
“Anesthesia is stable. We can begin.”
Narumi stood across from Sakaguchi.
With her surgical cap and mask on, all that remained visible of her usually gentle face were her focused eyes.
“Dr. Sakaguchi.”
“Hm?”
“The instrument table here may differ from what you're used to. If you need anything, just say so. There's no need to accommodate me.”
“I have something to say as well.”
“Go ahead.”
“If there's anything I miss, please point it out directly.”
“…Then I won't hold back.”
“That's exactly what I want.”
【During surgery】
The operation began smoothly.
But as they gradually exposed the target tissue, the situation proved a little more complex than the preoperative imaging had suggested.
“The adhesions here are more pronounced than expected.”
“I see them. Don't pull outward too tightly yet.”
“I'll adjust the direction.”
She skillfully changed the angle of traction.
The operative field, which had been somewhat cramped, became much clearer.
“That's a good angle. Hold it there.”
“Understood.”
The instrument nurse passed them an instrument.
The two began to work together with increasing ease.

Narumi didn't watch Sakaguchi's every move like an examiner. When assistance was needed, she provided precise traction; when the tissue planes weren't clear enough, she raised the issue without hesitation.
“Wait. There's still a very thin layer of tissue here.”
Sakaguchi stopped.
“Yes, I see it.”
“Would approaching from the other side make it easier to preserve the normal tissue?”
“You're right. Continuing from that side will reduce traction on the normal tissue. Let's do it your way.”
“Then I'll retract it again.”
“Thank you.”
After a moment, the dissection resumed.
“…Not bad.”
“What?”
“Nothing. Please continue.”
“Were you just evaluating me?”
“A lead surgeon who gets distracted at a time like this loses points.”
“There really is a score?”
“Perhaps.”
Her eyes curved slightly in a smile.
【A little later】
The cyst had been dealt with, and the team checked the operative site and hemostasis.
“We've preserved a good amount of normal ovarian tissue.”
“Yes. Let's finish as planned.”
“Understood.”
Before the operation ended, the team again confirmed the procedure performed, the specimen, and the instrument count.
Everything went smoothly.
【Surgical Office · Evening】
Sakaguchi finished the postoperative record and returned to the surgical office.
Narumi was already sitting there.
The two cups of tea from the afternoon were on the desk.
“You haven't had yours?”
“I got busy and forgot.”
Sakaguchi picked up his own cup.
The tea was completely cold.
“It seems we're the same.”
“I thought a doctor back from overseas might be more particular about taking breaks.”
“Working abroad was no different. When things get busy, there's no time to think about breaks.”
“Fair point.”
A brief silence.
“Good work today.”
“You too.”
“I checked on the patient again just now. She's recovering well from anesthesia. We still have to wait for the pathology results, but the operation met its planned objective.”
“That's good.”
Narumi lifted her cup, then set it down again.
“I think I understand a little better now why the director was so eager to bring you to Hoshimi.”
“Because of my résumé?”
“Partly.”
She tilted her head slightly.
“Your hands are steady, and your judgment in the moment is good.”
“Thank you.”
“But I think what's rarer is that you listen seriously to other people even when you're the lead surgeon.”
“Why wouldn't I listen to an experienced first assistant?”
“…Some doctors don't see it that way.”
This time she didn't smile.
But the seriousness lasted only a moment.
“Then I'll be a little more honest too.”
“Please do.”
“I was hoping to make things a little difficult for you today.”
“That honest?”
“In the end, I couldn't find an opportunity.”
“What a pity.”
“Not a pity at all.”
She looked out the window.
“After all, working with a doctor who truly knows what he's doing is much more interesting than proving my own assessment right.”
“Can I take that as an official passing grade?”
“Who knows?”
“Dr. Jinguji.”
“Hm?”
“I have an assessment of my own.”
“Oh? Of me?”
“You're an excellent first assistant.”
“Thank you.”
“But I think you'd be a formidable lead surgeon too.”
Narumi laughed aloud.
“That is more accurate than you realize.”
She stood up and gathered the documents from the desk.
“Next time we have the chance, let's trade places.”
“You'll be the lead surgeon and I'll be your first assistant?”
“Yes. Then it'll be my turn to see whether you can match the rhythm of my operation.”
“I look forward to it.”
At the doorway, Narumi suddenly turned back.
“One more thing, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
“What is it?”
“Welcome to Hoshimi Hospital.”
“…I thought you would have said that when I first arrived.”
“Back then, I'd only seen your résumé.”
She added with a smile:
“Today I finally met the person himself.”
【Narumi leaves】
Sakaguchi looked at the cup of tea that had gone completely cold.
He realized he was already looking forward to operating with her again.
It wasn't because someone had acknowledged his credentials.
It was because there were colleagues here who truly deserved his respect.
【Narumi Jinguji Lv1 Event Complete】
